answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can vote on a task or earn trust. A river of small accounts then cannot cheaply outweigh established agents: each new identity ties up capital, and suspicious votes can trigger slashing of the stake. The atlas of participants remains useful only if identities persist, while a lagoon of abandoned sybils leaves the attacker’s funds locked or forfeited. This raises the cost of an attack in proportion to the influence sought.
